title: Streaming exposes private runtime authority to its caller and inherited tasks

locations.description: _operation retains peer phase across yield at582
Audit uses ambient peer ContextVar as socket authority

trigger: Use supported_resident_client with synthetic config/auth and HTTP MockTransport, wrap it in ResidentInferenceAdapter, await first stream event, then create an asyncio child task and close the stream before releasing the child.
expected: Outside the owned client operation, caller and child task have no private phase; Path.home resolves to isolated state and caller-side socket policy events remain denied.
impact: A Python async generator yields in the consuming task context. The peer ContextVar survives the yield; create_task copies it. The copied phase remains accepted after owned stream cleanup. Thus caller-side endpoint socket policy and original-home resolution escape the intended private operation scope. This is a demonstrated isolation-policy bypass, not a claim of actual credential theft, native action or network dispatch.
verification: 4/17 supported-factory assertions fail in one R11 family; default caller denial, parent restoration, early close/caller cancellation, genuine fake auth delegation and factory cleanup controls pass. A separate direct-wrapper inert probe independently reproduces the yield leak.
recommendation: Restore the caller context before yielding events and prevent copied contexts from authorizing I/O once the owned operation closes. Add caller/inherited-task denial oracles to the existing private thread propagation tests. Preserve normal gate/lease, expiry, cancellation and raw failure receipts.
controls: No candidate edits, live model/native/real credentials/private data/network/outbound operations. Socket checks use sys.audit events only; transport is HTTP MockTransport, homes/auth/locks are synthetic.
full_audit_status: Other current full-scope evidence is preserved; this bounded finding artifact does not predeclare an overall nonblocking verdict.
merge_policy: User targets Wisp1.3.0 and forbids merging; PR remains draft.
